title: Enhancing CGRA Efficiency Through Aligned Compute and Communication Provisioning
problem: Existing CGRAs overprovision communication resources (routers consume 44% of power/area in spatio-temporal designs) relative to compute capabilities because each PE is paired with a full crossbar/router that handles peak congestion, resulting in low average communication utilization and wasteful programmability encoding.
motivation: Edge devices demand high-performance, energy-efficient, domain-agnostic accelerators; CGRA communication over-provisioning directly wastes 43% of power and 46% of area without providing proportional benefit to computational throughput.
method: Plaid observes that dataflow programs repeatedly use three-node communication patterns (fan-in, fan-out, unicast) and designs processor units (PCUs) where three arithmetic units (ALUs) share a single lightweight local router to handle these patterns, while a separate global router connects PCUs together. A compiler based on the Morpher toolchain, using simulated-annealing-based modulo scheduling (testing different arrangements and keeping the best), automatically identifies these patterns and maps them onto the PCU array. Implemented in 22nm FDSOI silicon at 100MHz, a 2x2 array of PCUs delivers 16 functional units—as much compute as a traditional 4x4 spatio-temporal architecture, but using far fewer routers.
key_novelty: Plaid groups three arithmetic units (ALUs) into processor units (PCUs) that share one lightweight local router—matching communication hardware to the repeating three-node dataflow patterns programs execute—replacing overprovisioned individual crossbars.
contributions: Identification of compute/communication misalignment as a fundamental CGRA efficiency bottleneck
Three-node structural motif abstraction as exhaustive DFG building blocks enabling collective routing
Plaid CGRA architecture with hierarchical two-level NoC (local intra-PCU + global inter-PCU routers)
End-to-end Plaid compiler with motif identification and hierarchical modulo-scheduling mapper

metrics.speedup: 1.4x performance improvement over energy-efficient spatial CGRA; same performance as high-performance spatio-temporal CGRA
metrics.energy_or_tops_w: 43% power reduction vs spatio-temporal CGRA; 27.7% energy reduction vs spatial CGRA; 42% total energy reduction vs spatio-temporal
metrics.area: 46% area savings vs spatio-temporal CGRA; 48% area savings vs spatial CGRA; CGRA fabric 33,366 um2 at 22nm
metrics.ppa: 1.22x energy efficiency and 1.25x area efficiency vs domain-optimized spatio-temporal CGRA
metrics.other: Evaluated on 30 DFGs from TinyML, PolyBench linear algebra, and image processing benchmarks

limitations: Performance degrades on kernels with very complex or long-distance data dependencies that cannot be captured by three-node motifs, requiring fallback to individual-node execution with global routing.
